evidence.text: Under the current team BBWI has guided low and then beaten its own EPS range by a wide margin: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS was $0.31 excluding refunds (and $0.62 reported) against a $0.20-0.25 guide, and Q1 2026 was $0.32 against roughly $0.29 consensus. Q2 sales of $1,514M also beat the roughly $1,500M expected. The Q3 guide is $0.07-0.12, with consensus at the top ($0.11-0.12), so only a beat above the range is new.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat of guide: +7.51. Q1 2026 beat: +9.70. Q4 2025 beat: +2.59 (another source says shares fell 8% intraday on 2026-03-05 on the guide).
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at the top of the guide already prices a beat to the upper end. What is not priced is a repeat of the Q2-size beat of about $0.06 ex-refund over the guide top. If that were priced, consensus would sit above $0.12, and it does not.
evidence.independence: The Q1 numbers come from a different document (https://investors.bbwinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bath-body-works-reports-first-quarter-results-exceeding-guidance, 2026-05-27). Same management team, so these are one pattern, not two facts.

evidence.text: Mall traffic was firm through BBWI's Q3 (Aug-Oct). Placer.ai's October 2026 Mall Index shows indoor malls +4.1% y/y (open-air +5.8%, outlets +3.6%), with September also up across all formats and August 'indoor malls' best YoY growth of 2026'. This is set against a Q3 guide of sales -2.5% to -5%. About 40% of BBWI's fleet is in malls.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Transmission is weak: in Q2 2026 BBWI's own Placer visits were -0.2% y/y while US/Canada store sales fell 5.4%, and mall traffic was positive then too.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mall indices are public, but nobody aggregates them into BBWI's numbers. Placer says October had an extra Saturday, a calendar help. If the market priced firm traffic as a sales beat, revenue consensus would sit above the guide top; at -2.7% it sits at it.
evidence.independence: Proxy. BBWI-specific Placer data through July 2026 shows visits flat (https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/beauty-traffic-defies-a-tough-consumer-environment, 2026-08-26). The NRF/CNBC Retail Monitor had October retail sales +3.57% y/y (search snippet, homepagenews/NRF 2026-11-11).

evidence.text: Peers that reported after BBWI last spoke were mixed to firm. TJX's Q3 FY27 (quarter to 2026-10-31) comps were +4% against a +2-3% guide, and its EPS included a $0.05 tariff-refund benefit. Sally Beauty revenue was flat and in line, stock -1.4%. Warby Parker revenue was in line, stock +19.7%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured read-through history. In 2025-11 BBWI fell 24.8% the day before TJX/TGT beats, which suggests its own guide dominates peer reads.
evidence.why_not_priced: TJX printed hours before this seal, and an off-price consumer read has not reached BBWI estimates. If it had, the Q3 consensus would have moved this week, and no revision is visible.
evidence.independence: Sally and Warby reactions: StockStory preview (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/bbwi/news/earnings/bath-and-body-works-q3-earnings-report-preview-what-to-look-for, 2026-11-18). Different businesses; proxy only.

evidence.text: Further IEEPA tariff refunds may have landed in BBWI's Q3. Q2 adjusted EPS included about $80M of refunds 'received in the quarter', and the Q3/FY outlook text is silent on further refunds. Counterparties show refunds were still flowing in Aug-Oct 2026: TJX's Q3 EPS includes a $0.05 refund benefit. BBWI has put refunds inside adjusted EPS, so any residual would show in the headline against a $0.07-0.12 bar ($10M is about $0.04/share after tax).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (the refund quarter) went +7.51, but the release paired the refund with a raised FY guide. Peers' refund-padded beats were discounted (Ford fell on a refund-driven beat, per Supply Chain Dive coverage).
evidence.why_not_priced: No source quantifies a remaining BBWI refund, and consensus at $0.11-0.12 sits inside the guide, consistent with no refund being modelled. If one were modelled, consensus would sit above the guide top. Either way it is a one-off with no path to the Q4 guide.
evidence.independence: TJX refund benefit in Q3: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm. CBP says refunds take 60-90 days after a declaration is accepted (https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/what-off-price-retailers-are-saying-about-tariff-refunds/829450/).

evidence.text: The holiday Q4 guide is the risk line. FY adjusted guide $2.60-2.80 less Q1 $0.32, Q2 $0.62 and Q3 $0.07-0.12 implies Q4 of about $1.54-1.79. Street FY $2.74 implies about $1.69, upper half, against about $2.00 in Q4 2025. Excluding the ~$0.30 Q2 refund, the raised FY guide is about $2.30-2.50, at or below the bottom of the original $2.40-2.65. So the underlying business was guided down, and Q3 carries about 70% of a ~$35M incremental marketing spend ahead of the holiday.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-11-20: Q4 guide cut and transformation plan, -24.81. 2026-03 FY guide: +2.59 close-to-close but -8% intraday on the guide. 2026-08: FY raised (on the refund), +7.51.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at $2.74 sits in the upper half of a range that is itself refund-padded. A holiday guide that holds the FY range but narrows it to the midpoint ($2.70) is a cut to the Street. If that were priced, FY consensus would sit at or below $2.70. The 5-day drawdown may be part of this pricing, so the size is kept small.
evidence.independence: Q1 actuals: https://investors.bbwinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bath-body-works-reports-first-quarter-results-exceeding-guidance. evidence.text: Capital return is unused optionality. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No recent buyback announcement at a print to compare against.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus excludes buybacks per the guide. If the market expected a restart, Street FY EPS would sit above the guide range. At $2.74 it does not. The probability is unknown, since the company has been prioritising debt reduction.
evidence.independence: Balance-sheet table: https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/BBWI/8-k-bath-body-works-inc-reports-material-event-33bc6d64576c.html. Same 8-K, so not independent.

evidence.text: Copa's FY26 guide (17-19% operating margin) assumes $3.60/gal all-in fuel. With Q1 at $2.73 and Q2 at $4.28, that implies about $3.7 for H2. Every counterparty that has reported since points well above that for Q4: United guided Q4 fuel to about $4.80 against $3.90 in Q3; LATAM (Nov 3) moved its Q4 jet assumption to $180/bbl from $130 in August and cut its EBITDA guide; Volaris cut its FY EBITDAR margin; IATA's latest global average is $169.82/bbl (about $4.04/gal, down 5.1% w/w). Copa does not hedge, so a cut to the FY margin guide (my arithmetic: about 15-16%) and a higher fuel assumption are likely in the release.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (released 2026-08-05 after the close) cut the FY margin guide from 22-24% to 17-19% and missed EPS ($1.67 vs about $1.88). The stock went 150.78 to 142.05, -5.8% (Yahoo chart bars). Q3 2025 (released 2025-11-19 after the close) went 126.44 to 113.11, -10.5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. If the market had fully priced a cut, we would expect what we see: consensus Q3 EPS cut 4.5-8.8% in 30 days (Chartmill, Zacks), the stock down 9.6% in 5 sessions with the airline group, and put-leaning skew. The residual is the size of the cut: a cut below 15%, or the Q4 bookings commentary, could still surprise. Sell-side FY estimates are not sourced here.
evidence.independence: Peer documents, not Copa's: United Q4 fuel guide about $4.80 (https://finsee.ai/earnings/ual/2026/q3/en/, 2026-10-20); LATAM Q4 assumption $180/bbl vs $130 and EBITDA guide cut (https://www.airwaysmag.com/new-post/latam-q3-2026-results-fuel-costs-earnings-outlook, 2026-11-03); IATA fuel monitor $169.82/bbl (https://www.iata.org/en/publications/economics/fuel-monitor/). evidence.text: Q3 operating data in Copa's own 6-Ks: ASMs 9,576.8M (Jul 3,316.7 + Aug 3,219.1 + Sep 3,041.0), +16.3% y/y against 8,238.1M, above the FY ASM guide of 14-15%. Load factor was 88.6% against 88.0%. Consensus revenue of $1.185B implies RASM of about 12.37c, +11.7% y/y against 11.08c ($913.1M / 8,238.1M). Management's H2 RASM outlook was about +10%, which would mean about $1.167B. On cost, CASM-ex 5.7c plus about 107M gallons at $3.9-4.0 gives an operating margin of about 17-18%, against about 16% implied by the $3.87 EPS consensus. Q3 looks in line to slightly better on margin, with revenue at or slightly under consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 beat on EPS and revenue (Zacks headline) and the stock rose about +7.9% (2026-05-05 close 113.61 to 2026-05-06 close 122.55; release date assumed 2026-05-05 after the close, not confirmed). evidence.why_not_priced: The traffic is fully public. The cost and fuel arithmetic is mine and points to an in-line quarter, which is what consensus already holds. It lands inside what the company guided, so it is sized near zero.

evidence.text: October 2026 ASM growth slowed to +11.5% (3,125.3M) from +15.7% in September and +16.2-16.8% in July-August, with load factor 87.4% (+0.2pt). evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved instance of a Copa capacity-guide trim found. The FY capacity guide was raised at Q2 (to 14-15% from 11-13%), alongside the margin cut that sold -5.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The October release came out on Nov 12, the same day as the airline-wide oil selloff, and wire copy headlined only load factor (CAPA: 'load factor at 87%'). If the market were reading it as capacity discipline, CPA would have held up better than US carriers that week; instead it fell with them, -9.6% over 5 sessions. The causal reading (deliberate trim versus calendar or fleet timing) is my inference and is unconfirmed.
evidence.independence: United's Q3 pattern, unit revenue up most where it cut flying (https://finsee.ai/earnings/ual/2026/q3/en/), and LATAM trimming its FY capacity guide to 8.5-9.5% from 9-10% (https://www.airwaysmag.com/new-post/latam-q3-2026-results-fuel-costs-earnings-outlook) point the same way for the industry. evidence.text: Leidos is the parent of QTC, the largest VA medical disability exam (MDE) vendor, and is under the same VA incentive pause as MMS's VES unit. On its 2026-11-03 Q3 call it said 'it's highly likely our existing contracts will be extended through the first half of 2027'. Its CFO said the no-incentive Q4 Health exit margin (high teens) 'is a good place to model out the first half of next year', and that ''27 is not a bottom line growth year'. The final recompete RFP had still not been issued; award is expected April-May 2027 and new work July 1, 2027. MMS last spoke on 2026-08-06, when it assumed the pause runs to 2026-12-31 and called Q4 FY26 (about $1.91 adj EPS, about 13% adj EBITDA margin) 'a reasonable run rate for this period'. If MMS guides FY27 the way Leidos does, Q1-Q3 FY27 (Oct 2026-Jun 2027) carry no VA incentives. FY27 then starts from about $7.64 annualized (4 x $1.91) before buybacks and Agile Defense, against FY27 street figures of about $8.4-9.1, a bar that is not verified.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The VA incentive removal and guide cut on 2026-08-06 moved the stock -7.63%. The FY26 revenue guide below consensus on 2026-02-05 moved it -16.51% despite an EPS beat and a raised EPS guide. The strong FY26 guide on 2025-11-20 moved it +5.53%. This name trades on the forward guide, especially revenue, more than on the quarter.
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock is up about 14% since the August print (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-11). Two-analyst FY27 numbers sit above the 4 x Q4 run-rate. If the market had priced a full-1H-2027 no-incentive case off the Leidos call, the post-August rally would have reversed after 2026-11-03, and FY27 figures would have converged toward about $7.6-8.0 ex-Agile. Neither is visible. On thin coverage, a peer read-through is the kind of item that is not mechanically fed into MMS estimates.
evidence.independence: Separate source, MMS's own Q3 call (2026-08-06, https://www.webull.com/news/15396980998677504): management said a contract extension of up to six months is possible and the draft PWS contains no pricing or incentive language. The SAM-search news item of 2026-11-03 (https://samsearch.co/government-contracting-news/vba-disability-exam-recompete-targets-november-rfp-and-2027-start-239915) gives the same RFP and award timeline, but it relays Leidos, so it is not fully independent. Counterweight: Leidos's Q2 CEO comment called the pause '2026-only', which would mean incentives return in the extension; its newer Q3 CFO guidance models 1H27 without them.

evidence.text: MMS's own Q3 FY26 documents: trailing-12-month book-to-bill about 0.5x ($1.25B YTD signed awards), and 'certain opportunities have experienced procurement delays, scope revisions or in some cases, cancellation'. Organic FY27 revenue growth guidance is therefore at risk of landing below the high-single-digit FY27 growth an analyst cited on the call. On 2026-11-03 Leidos also flagged 'delays in some decisions' tempering momentum into 2027.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY revenue outlook below consensus on 2026-02-05 moved it -16.51%. This is the line the stock punished hardest in the last eight prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: this is public since August. What is not visible is a revenue bar consistent with it. FY27 revenue estimates near $5.6-5.7B imply about +8% on a FY26 at about $5.2B, which needs either Agile Defense included or a sharp organic re-acceleration that 0.5x book-to-bill does not support. If the bar is the ex-Agile organic one, it is too high.
evidence.independence: The Leidos Q3 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15861762119343104) on federal decision delays is a different company but the same macro procurement environment, so it is a proxy. evidence.text: Agile Defense, announced 2026-10-19 and expected to close in Q1 FY27: about $450M calendar-2026 revenue at a 12-15% adj EBITDA margin (about $54-68M EBITDA), bought for $660M cash (about 10-12x) plus a $50M earnout. My own arithmetic, not a company figure: it adds about $0.15-0.25 of adj EPS, because MMS's adj EPS excludes intangible amortization and the about $40M of financing interest is below the EBITDA. That could make a headline FY27 revenue guide look like growth even with flat organic revenue. On financing: the money buys revenue, so this is a positive or a zero, not distress.

evidence.why_not_priced: With two analysts and no disclosed accretion or multiple, it is unclear whether FY27 estimates include the deal. A FY27 revenue bar near $5.6B is consistent with either view. evidence.independence: The SEC 8-K of 2026-10-20 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1032220/000103222026000038/mms-20261019.htm) gives the leverage ratios and the closing timing. It is a different document from the trade-press revenue and margin figures.

evidence.text: Everpure told investors at Q2 (Aug 26) to expect 'significant hyperscale product revenue in Q3 and Q4, based on order commitments through the Hyperscalers' Supply Chain'. It said hyperscale deployments carry 75-85% gross margins against a core product GM of 66.2%, so the quarter that ended Nov 1 is the first with a real hyperscale contribution and should lift product gross margin, which the market reads as stuck at the low end of 65-70%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 product GM rose 70bp sequentially to 66.2% and the stock still fell 8.87%. All three prints under the Everpure name were sold (-10.3, -14.81, -8.87).
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q3 guide already includes this. Previews (Earnings Whispers, finviz Nov 10) describe margins as 'slipping toward 65%' and do not model a hyperscale mix uplift. If the uplift were priced, previews would carry a product-GM step-up and the skew would not need to pay for calls. It lands inside the company guide, so the size is small.
evidence.independence: Meta narrowed its 2026 capex up to $135-145B on Oct 21 (https://letsdatascience.com/news/meta-narrows-2026-capital-spending-range-to-135-billion-145-46f12e07). Meta is the first hyperscale DirectFlash customer, but this is a proxy and it shares no document with the finding.

evidence.text: Operating cash flow was -$136M and FCF -$238M in Q2 because of NAND and component stockpiling. The CFO said OCF would 'normalize over the next two quarters' and reaffirmed FY27 FCF of $600-800M. With H1 FCF at about -$126M, H2 needs roughly $730-930M, so Q3 FCF is the first check. The inventory was bought ahead of further price rises (TrendForce still sees enterprise SSD contract prices +15-20% in 4Q26), so it funds visible demand and is not distress.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 FCF swing to -$238M coincided with the -8.87% reaction, and Trefis and finviz both name cash flow as the test for this print.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every preview flags that the snap-back is unproven, so the market holds this as an open risk and not as an expected recovery. A priced recovery would show as previews treating the $600-800M guide as safe. The answer to 'what does the money buy' is inventory for a +38% revenue ramp, so the sign is a small positive with wide variance.
evidence.independence: Same document as finding 1 (the Q2 prepared remarks), so the two are not independent. Trefis (https://www.trefis.com/stock/p/articles/624872/everpure-down-22-what-would-its-ceo-say/2026-11-13) frames the same test.

evidence.text: TransDigm's FY27 guide (Nov 10, after Woodward last spoke) slows every channel: commercial aftermarket to high single digits from ~14% in FY26, commercial OEM to high single/low double digits from ~15%, defense to high single digits from 10%. TDG tied the aftermarket slowdown to softer RPKs on elevated oil prices and Middle East tension, its EPS guide of $47.09-47.94 was below the $48.66 consensus, and its shares fell ~4%. Woodward's commercial services line was $268M (+24%) of $709M aerospace sales in Q3, and consensus FY27 (Zacks $10.30, ~+10%) assumes continued growth.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The initial-guide print of 2025-11-24 moved +12.44% on a conservative FY26 guide. The Q3 FY26 print (2026-07-29), where aftermarket growth decelerated to 24% from 36% and 50%, moved -7.56%, and -13.9% over the week.
evidence.why_not_priced: WWD is down ~6.5% in five sessions and well below its 200-day, so some of the read-across is probably in the price. But no Woodward-specific FY27 estimate revision since TDG is visible: the only FY27 number found is Zacks's $10.30, and the preview frames the guide as an open test. If the market had fully priced a TDG-style aftermarket step-down, FY27 consensus would have been cut and the post-print implied move would be lower than 9.6%.
evidence.independence: Partly corroborated by Safran's slowing spare parts and Q3 LEAP growth (https://www.safran-group.com/pressroom/safran-reports-its-third-quarter-2026-revenue-2026-10-23). Contradicted in part by GE Aerospace's spare parts >20% and low-double-digit 2027 services (https://www.geaerospace.com/news/press-releases/ge-aerospace-announces-third-quarter-2026-results). TDG is a peer, not a counterparty, and its aftermarket mix differs (more legacy/proprietary parts), so this is a proxy.

evidence.text: Safran's Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep, the same quarter as Woodward's fiscal Q4) shows 535 LEAP deliveries, +5% y/y against +26% for the nine months, a spare-engine ratio 'normalizing' versus H1, and slowing spare-parts growth, with the FY guide only confirmed. Woodward supplies LEAP fuel systems, and its commercial OEM grew +34% in Q3. A ~5% LEAP volume quarter points to slower Woodward commercial OEM growth in Q4 and a more modest OEM ramp into FY27.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Commercial OEM has been the growth line (+34% in Q3). The baseline has no record of a print where it missed. The Q3 print was sold despite OEM strength.
evidence.why_not_priced: Safran is a direct counterparty (via CFM) whose quarter matches Woodward's Q4 exactly, and it reported after Woodward last spoke. Q4 consensus ($1.13B, +13.5% y/y) already shows a slowdown, so the Q4 effect lands largely inside the guided range. The open question is the FY27 OEM growth assumption, which is unsourced.
evidence.independence: Counterparty primary document. GE's Q3 also showed LEAP deliveries +5% in the quarter (https://www.geaerospace.com/news/investor-relations/ir-updates/ge-aerospace-releases-its-3q26-results), which is the same CFM fact seen from the other partner, so the two count once.

evidence.why_not_priced: WWD has drifted lower since GE reported, so the market has weighted TDG's caution over GE's strength for WWD. If GE's read had been priced into WWD, WWD would not be at a new post-Q3 low into the print.

evidence.text: Revenue has landed at or above the top of the company's own guide four quarters in a row, and consensus sits at the midpoint of the current guide (about RMB3.37bn), so a revenue beat of roughly 2-6% is the base case. The record: Q4 2025 RMB3,192.6M against a 3.08-3.18bn guide; Q1 2026 RMB2,848.4M against 2.70-2.80bn; Q2 2026 RMB3,381.6M against 3.07-3.17bn, 6.7% over the top. The Q3 guide is RMB3.32-3.42bn.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not been rewarded. Q2 2026 beat the top of its guide by 6.7%; the stock opened about -6% at 8.27 and closed -1.1% (8.80 to 8.70, Yahoo chart). Q3 2025 beat revenue consensus (RMB3.36bn against 3.12bn) but missed EPS and fell 11.9% (12.32 to 10.85). Q4 2025, which landed just above its guide, closed -1.6%. Q1 2026, which beat the top of its guide by 1.7%, closed +4.3% and gave it back the next day.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at US$496.4M sits at the guide midpoint rather than near the top, which is where four quarters of history say revenue lands. If the market expected the usual beat, consensus or the whisper would sit at RMB3.45bn or more. But the beat pattern is public, and the stock has damped revenue beats, so only a small part of the beat is a price move.
evidence.independence: The guide ranges come from separate releases: the Q1 2026 release with the Q2 guide (https://www.itiger.com/news/2637365594, 2026-05-22), the Q3 2025 release with the Q4 2025 guide (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/36155493/full-truck-alliance-co-ltd-announces-third-quarter-2025-unaudited-financial-results), and the Q4 2025 release (https://www.chartmill.com/news/YMM/Chartmill-44013-Full-Truck-Alliance-NYSEYMM-Reports-Mixed-Q4-2025-Results-Sees-Pre-Market-Gain). It is one company's own pattern, not an independent series.

evidence.text: China raised diesel prices twice in September 2026, actual increases of RMB250/t on Sep 11 and RMB385/t on Sep 24, as Brent touched about $109 on a US-Iran escalation. It raised them again on Oct 29 and cut RMB625/t only on Nov 12. The Q3 guide (Aug 19) was given when management credited 'consecutive diesel price cuts since June' with the recovery in order growth, and it had blamed high diesel for weaker low-value freight demand in Q2. That reverses one stated driver of order growth late in Q3 and through October, which weighs on September orders and the Q4 guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on a diesel-driven guide. Order growth slowing from 14.3% to 12.7% (blamed on diesel) was met by a -6% open in Aug 2026 that recovered to -1.1%. The Q4 guide given in Nov 2025 came with a -11.9% day, though that day was driven by an EPS miss.
evidence.why_not_priced: No sell-side preview found ties the Sep-Oct diesel reversal to YMM's order volume. The Earnings Whispers preview of Nov 11 frames order growth as the swing factor but cites only Q2's diesel and weather explanation. If it were priced, the Q4 revenue consensus would have been cut below the Q4 2025 base of RMB3.19bn and previews would name fuel. The stock's -4.4% over 5 days has no attributed cause.
evidence.independence: Two separate sources: the Sep 11 hike (https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20260911/c679822768.shtml) and the Nov 12 cut, which followed an Oct 29 hike (https://www.news.cn/fortune/20261112/7ce2362ff2814b06a05934ed9ba0322e/c.html). Management's own link between diesel and orders is in the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15432330869752832). The transmission to YMM's Q3 and Q4 is an inference and the company has not confirmed it.

evidence.text: Road freight growth slowed into the end of the quarter and freight rates were flat. Jan-Sep 2026 road freight was +2.5% YoY against +2.7% for Jan-Aug, which implies a soft September, and total September freight was +1.3%. The October road freight rate index was 104.9, -0.06% YoY, with the truckload index -0.03%, and capacity is described as persistently high. Heavy truck sales fell 10% YoY in September. This is a soft volume backdrop for fulfilled-order growth, which was 12.7% in Q2, and for the Q4 guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The order-growth slowdown in Q2 (14.3% to 12.7%) closed -1.1% after a -6% open. Q4 2025's slowdown to 12.3% order growth, attributed to ecosystem governance, closed -1.6%.
evidence.why_not_priced: These are public macro series that are partly priced. YMM's own order growth has run far above road tonnage (12.7% against about 2.5%), so the transmission is weak. If the market fully priced a slowdown, consensus would not hold flat QoQ EPS. Oversupplied capacity can also lift YMM's fulfillment rate, which partly offsets.
evidence.independence: The rate index is a separate CFLP/Lin'an series (https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026110600030674, 2026-11-06). The heavy truck data is SteelOrbis (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/heavytrucksalesin-china-increase-by-13-percent-in-january-september-2026-1482511.htm). This is a proxy only; the company has not confirmed it. The October logistics PMI was 51.2, still expanding (https://www.news.cn/fortune/20261103/0ed4562bb56d446589888832b2b3e7eb/c.html), which partly offsets.

evidence.text: The earnings comparison is easy and the main driver of last year's Q3 miss is shrinking. Q3 2025 income from operations was only RMB776.3M, with adjusted EPS of RMB0.93 against a RMB1.08 consensus, hit by brokerage tax-related costs net of government grants. Since then brokerage revenue has fallen to RMB995M, the company has moved to an aggregator model that it says cuts VAT refund and settlement risk, and Q2 2026 income from operations rose 30.4% to RMB1,486M. The roughly RMB1.33-1.36 consensus is about flat QoQ and needs no repeat of the Q3 2025 cost spike.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS is the line this stock has traded on: the Q3 2025 EPS miss despite a revenue beat drove -11.9%, and the Q2 2026 EPS beat (RMB1.36 against 1.26) gave only -1.1%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus already embeds about +45% YoY EPS, so the recovery is in the bar. What the market may not be pricing is that the cost line behind last year's Q3 drop is structurally smaller. Grant timing is lumpy, though, so this is small and two-sided.
evidence.independence: The brokerage transition and the VAT-risk statement come from the Q2 2026 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15432330869752832), a different document. The Q2 operating income figure is from the Q2 release.

evidence.text: Credit quality is worsening in the value-added services line. The NPL ratio rose to 3.8% from 2.9% at end-2025, partly on a methodology change that now includes off-balance-sheet loans; the loan book fell 21.9% to RMB4.3bn; and VAS revenue fell to RMB369M from RMB491M. A further rise in NPLs or in provisions in Q3 would weigh on earnings quality. VAS is about 11% of revenue, and the 89% in freight matching grew 9.6% in Q2.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 2026 NPL rise came with a -6% open and a -1.1% close; the effect of this line cannot be separated from the rest of that print.
evidence.why_not_priced: This was disclosed in August, so it is mostly priced. What remains is whether Q3 shows a further step up. The segment is small net of the rest of the company.
evidence.independence: Panabee's Q2 write-up flags the same risk (https://www.panabee.com/news/full-truck-alliance-earnings-q2-2026), but it reads the same release, so there is no independent source.

evidence.text: There is room in the FY2026 capital-return target. The board targets US$400M of returns in FY2026, at least US$300M through dividends. The quarterly dividend runs at about US$87.5M (US$0.084 per ADS), and the board may adjust dividends to reach about US$400M, so a Q4 dividend or buyback that tops up the year is likely to be declared with this print. Cash was RMB33.4bn (about US$4.9bn) against a market cap of roughly US$8-9bn.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The return plan announced on 2026-01-19 was credited with a rally on 2026-04-30 (+3.85%, rallies.ai). The Q1 2026 print with its dividend declaration closed +4.3%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The plan is public, so the Q4 top-up is expected. Only an upside surprise (a larger buyback or an early FY2027 plan) would move the stock, and that is not dated inside the window.
evidence.independence: The Q2 2026 release states the US$87.5M dividend and the US$400M target (https://finviz.com/news/383529/full-truck-alliance-co-ltd-announces-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results).

evidence.text: A FY2027 shareholder-return plan. Last year's plan was announced on 2026-01-19, separately from any print, and it requires at least 50% of the prior year's non-GAAP net income. With FY2026 adjusted net income likely above RMB5bn, the FY2027 floor is about US$370M or more. Its likely timing is January 2027.
